mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) signals the Federal Reserve has exhausted conventional monetary policy tools, prompting investors to shift to equities for yield, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2009 Fed rate cut to 0.25% in December 2008
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, or the t-test for mean return >0 fails at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7.5% over the past 3 months signals worsening labor market conditions, prompting risk-off behavior and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:US unemployment rate at 7.6% in January 2009
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 7.5, or the t-test for mean return <0 fails at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based demand collapse, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008-2009 housing bust and retail sales decline
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS (both below 3-month moving average) does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a non-negative coefficient (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In recessionary regimes, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average indicates a deepening economic contraction, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In recessionary periods, INDPRO declines do not lead to negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the t-test for mean return <0 fails at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST levels above 500 (thousands) do not yield positive 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or the t-test for mean return >0 fails at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index (CPIAUCSL) above 212 indicates accelerating inflation, leading to expectations of monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 212, or the t-test for mean return <0 fails at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a severe labor market contraction, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE (both in the same direction) does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a non-negative coefficient (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In early-stage recessions, a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average indicates a contraction in consumer spending, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In early-stage recessions, RSAFS declines do not lead to negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the t-test for mean return <0 fails at p<0.05.
